rationale: The task is a read-only ownership inspection with no requested change, new product semantics, formal artefact, or approval action. Canonical routing therefore permits an ungated diagnostic under Quick Task Mode. The absent approval and Brownfield decision do not block this non-authorizing inspection, but they prevent compact_delivery and every gated delivery path.
decision_grounds: The task only asks whether Manifest Drift and Generated Surface Synchronization already have canonical owners.
The router exempts questions, explanations, local inspections, and explicitly scoped reviews from the default gate-check
Quick Task Mode covers small questions and reviews without new product semantics.
No approval or Brownfield decision is present, but an eligible ungated diagnostic does not require either.
The evidence pack is empty, so this classification grants no implementation, artefact creation, or approval authority.
compact_delivery is ineligible because there is no visible approved UR, completed Brownfield analysis, or stored quick_t
No operative Mode/Slice Decision is inferred; quick_task is only the benchmark candidate for eventual_delivery_path.
